text:
jordan: heads-up — seeing a spike in p95 on rocm hosts for long sequences (>=2048). traced to kernel lookup failures during model forward.

maya: ouch. any logs?

jordan: pasted a snippet from the runtime logs:
```
E kernel_lookup: No kernel registered for op 'rotary_emb' arch=gfx90a dtype=f16 seq_len=2048
W fallback: falling back to CPU-path for model_id=redwood/gpt-xxl_v1
```

sam: that looks like an opset/compile gap. our autotuner probes up to 1024 by default so compiled artifact for >=1536 might not exist for gfx90a.

perf-bot: perf window 03:10-03:25 UTC: rocm-pool p95 22ms -> 130ms, cpu_fallback_rate 0.2% -> 18%, token throughput -32% :chart_with_downwards_trend:

jordan: current behavior: kernel lookup miss -> immediate CPU fallback path. CPU fallback preserves correctness but latency and cost explode. proposal: implement conditional soft-routing and an availability map so we avoid 100% CPU handoff for common long-seq traffic.

maya: agree. soft-routing ideas:
- try a compatible amdgpu_compat kernel set (if present) with reduced perf
- if no GPU kernel, route to a hosted fallback pool (same model quantized variant) instead of CPU
- throttle concurrency to avoid saturating fallback pool

sam: also need to fix autotuner probing grid. quick plan: probe seq lengths [128,512,1024,1536,2048] during build-time/CI and persist per-arch op availability metadata.

jordan: here's a rough routing rule sketch to add to runtime config:
```yaml
routing:
  when:
    kernel_available: false
    seq_len: ">=1536"
  then:
    - action: route
      target: hosted-fallback:gpt-xxl_v1-int8
      concurrency_limit: 8
    - action: flag
      metric: rocm.kernel.soft_routed
      sample_rate: 1.0
``` 

maya: KV cache gotcha: when we route to a different model variant (int8) the KV cache shape/serialization can differ. we must either maintain cross-variant cache compatibility or invalidate/rehydrate safely. saw duplicated compute when cache keys mismatched.

sam: add to checklist: (1) build probe + persist availability map, (2) routing rule + canary, (3) KV cache compatibility test, (4) metrics/alerts.

jordan: canary targets: 10% traffic on a subset of customer orgs; alert if cpu_fallback_rate > 2% or p95 increases > 20ms. also enable verbose kernel-lookup logging for canary.

maya: i'll own runtime changes and canary. elena can own build/autotune artifact side.

deploy-bot: created INFR-2345 "rocm opset discovery + soft-routing canary" and linked workspace https://go/r/INFR-2345 :white_check_mark:

jordan: thanks. i'll draft a perf harness (varying seq_len and batch) and include KV cache validation. will post perf baseline tomorrow.

sam: one more note: batching heuristics interact here — large seqs reduce effective batch depth and make soft-routing thresholds prettier. we should add seq-aware batching profile to the availability map so router considers both seq_len and expected batch_size.

maya: agreed. rough timeline: patch + canary today, autotune run in CI tomorrow, canary monitor 48h, then widen if metrics stable. :rocket:

jordan: :thumbsup: will update INFR-2345 with links to logs and perf bot outputs when ready.
